principles.title: Design principles
principles.hint: Phases receive the guidance of the active principles, tailored to their task. The instructions you write stay unchanged.

prompt.header:
# Design principles
This workflow follows the principles below. Apply them in your task; the general rules and the phase instructions take precedence in case of conflict. If a principle leads you to rule out a solution, say so in the result.

kiss.name: KISS (Keep It Simple)
kiss.summary: The simplest solution that solves the real problem.
kiss.analisi:
- Among the possible solutions, propose the one with the fewest moving parts; if you suggest a more complex one, explain which concrete requirement makes it necessary.
- Name the smallest change that solves the problem as the first step.
kiss.implementazione:
- Write direct, readable code: no abstraction layers, patterns or configuration the task does not need.
- Prefer short functions, clear names and linear flow over clever solutions.
- Use the tools and libraries already in the project before adding new ones.
kiss.test: - Keep tests simple and readable: one behaviour per test, minimal test data, no unnecessary test infrastructure.
kiss.revisione:
- Flag unjustified complexity: single-use abstractions, indirection, superfluous configuration or generalisation.
- For each finding, propose the simpler version.
kiss.personalizzata: - Choose the simplest way to do the task and avoid unnecessary steps or structures.
kiss.checklist: KISS: is the solution as simple as possible? Are there abstractions, layers or configuration that could be removed?

yagni.name: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
yagni.summary: Only what is needed now: no features or extensions for hypothetical needs.
yagni.analisi:
- Limit the plan to what the goal asks for; list ideas that were not requested separately, as possible future work.
- Do not plan extension points, options or generalisations without a current use case.
yagni.implementazione:
- Implement only the requested behaviour: no parameters, options, hooks or generic cases "for the future".
- Do not add unused code, interfaces with a single implementation or configuration nobody uses.
yagni.test: - Test the requested and existing behaviour; do not write tests for features that do not exist.
yagni.revisione:
- Flag code, options or generalisations the current goal does not need, and any dead code introduced.
- Suggest what to remove.
yagni.personalizzata: - Do only what the task requires, with no anticipatory additions.
yagni.checklist: YAGNI: was anything added that the goal did not ask for (options, extensions, unused code)?

dry.name: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
dry.summary: Every piece of knowledge has a single source in the code, without premature abstractions.
dry.analisi:
- Look in the project for existing functions, components or constants that solve part of the problem and recommend reusing them.
- Point out where the change risks duplicating logic that already exists.
dry.implementazione:
- Before writing new code, check whether something reusable already exists.
- Do not duplicate rules, values or logic: extract into a single place what truly repeats with the same meaning.
- Do not merge code just because it looks alike: if two parts can change for different reasons, keep them separate.
dry.test: - Reuse existing test helpers and fixtures; avoid setup blocks copied between tests.
dry.revisione:
- Flag duplicated logic, values or rules introduced by the change, pointing to where the original already exists.
- Also flag forced abstractions that tie together code with different meanings.
dry.personalizzata: - Reuse what already exists and avoid repeating the same information in several places.
dry.checklist: DRY: does the change duplicate logic or values already in the project? Does it reuse what existed?

solid.name: SOLID
solid.summary: Single responsibility, open/closed, substitutability (Liskov), small interfaces, depending on abstractions.
solid.analisi:
- Identify the responsibilities involved and where each part of the change belongs.
- Point out classes or modules that already do too much and whether the change would make them worse.
solid.implementazione:
- Each class, module or function has one responsibility and one reason to change.
- Extend behaviour by adding code rather than riskily changing stable code, where the project allows it.
- Subclasses and implementations honour the contract of the base type.
- Prefer small, specific interfaces; make high-level code depend on abstractions, not on details.
- Apply these principles in proportion: do not add interfaces or layers where a simple function is enough.
solid.test: - Test each responsibility in isolation; where needed, replace dependencies through their abstractions.
solid.revisione:
- Flag concrete violations: classes with several responsibilities, direct dependencies on details, implementations that break the contract, oversized interfaces.
- For each one, give a fix proportionate to the problem.
solid.personalizzata: - Keep each part of the work focused on a single responsibility.
solid.checklist: SOLID: does each module have a single responsibility? Do dependencies go through abstractions without needless layers?
